rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Food chain: Producer (TL1) → Primary consumer (TL2) → Secondary consumer (TL3) → Tertiary consumer (TL4)
10% rule: only ~10% of energy transfers between trophic levels
GPP = total photosynthesis; NPP = GPP − plant respiration (R)

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Grassland food chain: grass → rabbit → fox → eagle (4 trophic levels).  ·  Pond food web: algae → mosquito larva → frog → snake → eagle; also algae → zooplankton → small fish → big fish.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Detailed notes on 02 food chain food web trophic level ecological pyramids productivity within the ecology unit.  ·  Food chain: a linear sequence of organisms where each is eaten by the next; transfers energy and matter (sun → producer → primary consumer → secondary consumer → tertiary consumer).  ·  Food web: a network of interconnected food chains; more realistic than a single chain; shows multiple feeding relationships.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: 10% rule  ·  GPP and NPP  ·  Inverted pyramids

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Productivity  ·  In an ecosystem one can observe the transfer or flow of energy from one trophic level to other trophic level by the process of eating and being eaten.  ·  It forms a linear chain called food chain.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: There are basically three types of food chain in nature: 1.  ·  Grazing food chain: The food chain that starts from the green plants and ends to carnivores (top consumer) by passing though herbivores.  ·  Detritus food chain: The organic wastes and dead matter derived from grazing food chain are called as detritus.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Pyramid of energy: always upright; each level < the one below  ·  • Productivity  ·  Food chain = linear; food web = network of chains.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Trophic levels: TL1 producers, TL2 herbivores, TL3 carnivores, TL4+ top carnivores.  ·  Three pyramids: number, biomass, energy.  ·  Pyramid of energy is ALWAYS upright; number and biomass can be inverted.
